title: Nerve Fibre Morphometry with Transmission Electron Microscopy Using the Nucleator Probe
author: Kumar, Sharma, et al.

steps.title: Prepare Araldite resin mixture
steps.instruction: Mix 25 ml Araldite CY212 resin with 2 ml Dodecenyl Succinic Anhydride (DDSA, catalog D025), 1.8 ml Methyl Nadic Anhydride (MNA, catalog M012) and 0.9 ml 2,4,6‑Tri(dimethylaminomethyl) Phenol‑30 (DMP‑30, catalog D022) to a final volume of 50.9 ml.

steps.title: Primary fixation of nerve
steps.instruction: Immediately immerse the 2 mm‑long cochlear nerve segment in chilled fixative (4 °C) containing 2 % paraformaldehyde and 2.5 % glutaraldehyde in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) for 48 hours.

steps.title: Wash after primary fixation
steps.instruction: Wash the tissue three times in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) for 15 minutes each at 4 °C.

steps.title: Secondary fixation
steps.instruction: Post‑fix in 1 % osmium tetroxide prepared in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) for 1 hour at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash after secondary fixation
steps.instruction: Wash again three times in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) for 15 minutes each at 4 °C.

steps.title: Dehydrate tissue
steps.instruction: Pass the sample through graded acetone at 4 °C: 30 % acetone (15 min), 50 % (15 min), 70 % (15 min), 90 % (15 min), 100 % acetone twice (15 min each), then dry acetone 15 min at 4 °C followed by 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Clear tissue in toluene
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample in two changes of toluene, 30 minutes each at room temperature.

steps.title: Infiltrate with resin
steps.instruction: Infiltrate sequentially: (i) toluene + resin 3:1 for 1 hour at RT; (ii) toluene + resin 2:2 overnight at RT; (iii) toluene + resin 1:3 for 1 hour at RT under vacuum (380 mm Hg); (iv) pure resin for 2 hours at 45 °C under vacuum (380 mm Hg).

steps.title: Embed tissue in resin
steps.instruction: Place the infiltrated tissue in pure resin within an embedding mould at room temperature, keeping relative humidity below 50 %.

steps.title: Polymerise resin blocks
steps.instruction: Polymerise the moulds for 1 day at 50 °C, then continue at 60 °C until the resin is solid; verify completion using blank resin blocks without tissue.

steps.title: Trim and cut semithin sections
steps.instruction: Trim the polymerised block and cut transverse semithin sections 0.5 µm thick on an ultramicrotome (Ultracut UC7, Leica).

steps.title: Mount semithin sections
steps.instruction: Place sections on a drop of distilled water on a clean glass slide and adhere by warming on a hot plate at 80 °C.

steps.title: Stain semithin sections
steps.instruction: Apply a few drops of 1 % aqueous toluidine blue to the sections on the hot plate for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Wash and select area
steps.instruction: Wash the slide with distilled water, dry it, and examine under a light microscope to choose the region for ultrathin sectioning.

steps.title: Cut ultrathin sections
steps.instruction: Cut silver‑coloured ultrathin sections (~70 nm) from the block on the ultramicrotome.

steps.title: Collect sections on grids
steps.instruction: Pick the ultrathin sections onto 300‑mesh copper grids.

steps.title: Stain grids with uranyl acetate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge uranyl acetate solution, place 50 µl on parafilm in a Petri dish, float the grid (section side down) on the droplet, cover, incubate 10–15 min, then wash each grid with double‑distilled water.

steps.title: Stain grids with lead citrate
steps.instruction: In a laminar‑flow hood, place a droplet of alkaline lead citrate on parafilm, float the grid (section side down) on it, incubate 5–10 min, wash briefly in 0.02 M NaOH then twice in double‑distilled water.

steps.title: Dry stained grids
steps.instruction: Dry the grids on filter paper and allow them to air‑dry.

steps.title: Examine grids by TEM
steps.instruction: Observe the stained grids using a transmission electron microscope (FEI, Netherlands).
